## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_食神 (Wood carrying The Artisan). Persona The Artisan (食神). Definition line: "Output that flows from you, giving that feels like being". Keyword Flow, charge gentle, poles catalyst Grace / friction Coasting. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: giving that feels like being; worth tangled with what is made. Arena: craft, hands, the table, warmth of making, fed and feeding. Classical portrait: ease and appetite; output that flows without assertion; generous, content, prone to drift and indulgence. Ruled domains: Expression, Enjoyment, Children. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 伤官.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Water. structural_interaction seed: "Water generating Wood same-polarity — depth as natural source of effortless reach".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Artisan: growth that fruits. Everything you tend produces, gardens, projects, people, and the producing feels less like work than like season. You nourish by cultivating: patient feeding, honest pruning, harvests shared at the fence. Your gift ripens on its own schedule. Respect the schedule."
- k2_functional: "Your words grow on people slowly and stay. You persuade the way spring does."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Overripe","Lax","Overbooked"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Expression":"Your expression bears fruit: gardens, meals, projects that people can taste and hold. Make output a rhythm rather than an event. An orchard produces because producing is simply what it does.","Enjoyment":"You enjoy abundance in its natural forms: tables full, gardens loud, seasons honored with their own pleasures. Guard the fallow time too. Delight, like soil, needs its resting years.","Children":"You are patient with children and students. You feed them, give them space, and let them grow at their own speed rather than yours, and you enjoy the raising more than the results."}

- Sibling cell 木_伤官 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your expression grows wherever it wants, and forcing it into rows kills it. Give you a template and the life drains out. Give you open ground and something appears that nobody planted, better than what was planned, impossible to have ordered in advance."

Core element Water, energy element Wood. Law: Water feeds Wood (水生木: rain raises the forest). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Wood is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Water core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Expression is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 水_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Giving comes before being asked, for you. You feel most yourself with something to hand over, so you give ahead of knowing whether anyone needs it. Keep giving first, and accept that some of it reaches no one who needed it.

value_b.text: You give before anyone has to ask. Being the one with something to offer feels safer than being the one in need, and that puts giving ahead of waiting to be wanted. Give first, and notice when the giving starts to replace the wanting.

value.text: Giving first is how you make sure you matter. Because you would rather give than receive, you hardly ever let anyone give to you. Let one person carry you this week, and you get back the rest that giving first keeps taking.

value.text: You are always making something, and the making matters more than the result. Busy hands keep you steady, and you start the next thing rather than show the last. Keep making, and show one finished thing for every three you start.

value_b.text: Making things is your resting state. Because you trust your hands more than your words, you answer most questions with something made. Keep answering that way, and allow a made thing its slower understanding.

value.text: Stopping feels like disappearing, and making keeps you here. Starting the next thing is easier than being judged on the last, so you make instead of standing by. Stay beside a finished thing until praise comes, since the credit you never collect is the cost.

value.text: You stay relaxed on purpose. Enjoying what is in front of you matters more than getting ahead, and good enough is good enough for you. When you add one push to all that calm, you lose almost nothing to staying relaxed.

value_b.text: Staying relaxed is your natural speed. You would rather enjoy a thing than finish it fast, even on the days that want the other one. If you stay relaxed and meet the one deadline that matters, you keep both.

value.text: Staying relaxed is how you keep life good. Pushing feels like spoiling the day, and you take the comfortable choice rather than the forward one. Pick the harder one once a season, and you lose fewer chances to the comfort of staying relaxed.

value.text: Relaxed is how you run things for those in your care. Since you would rather be enjoyed than obeyed, you let a child or student set their own pace. Hold firm now and then, because you owe them a push along with your patience.
